display.purpose: The single health status word in the notifier pane; one per screen at most.

headline.purpose: Page heads and the alert-detail title; 24px on the sign-in card.

title-pane.purpose: Pane and feed heads; 15px for the verdict box head.

body.purpose: Default text, inputs, quoted replies; reasons at 15px, 72ch measure.

body-sm.purpose: Rows, chips, controls, table cells, captions.

label.purpose: Meta, table heads, fact labels; ink-3 or ink-4, sentence case.

label-rail.purpose: Rail item labels and river lane labels.

data.purpose: Times, IDs, ticket numbers, axis ticks, scores, key hints. Never prose.

themes.note: Both themes define the same custom-property names; frontmatter keys ending in -day are the light-theme values of the same property. on-ok (#04201c) is the same in both.

lightCore.purpose: 1.5px inset ring at 55% that gives river lights an edge against the pale day ground.

blur.name: float
blur.purpose: Tooltips and the sticky feed head, over glass-strong.

shadows.name: pane-lift-night
shadows.purpose: Glass panes and tooltips, dark theme.

shadows.name: pane-lift-day
shadows.purpose: Glass panes and tooltips, light theme.

shadows.name: light-halo
shadows.purpose: Glow on live dots, pips and timeline markers in their signal colour.

shadows.name: score-marker
shadows.purpose: Probability marker on the score bar.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Lights, trails, streaks and field bokeh slide between 5s re-renders.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Arrival of new lights (1.6s), new feed rows (1.2s), the theme knob (0.35s).

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Background and colour on rows, rail items and buttons; 0.15s for button press.

motion.name: sharpen
motion.purpose: Light hover: blur, opacity and scale.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Drift, arrival, breathe and shimmer all stop.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Panes to two columns; detail stacks; verdict box un-sticks.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes a 64px bottom bar; 16px gutter; panes stack; feed rows reflow.

narrative.overview:
Night-shift city light trails seen through frosted glass. The notifier's real traffic (every check, every alert from the last hour) moves behind the interface as light: a passing light per check, a red tail-light streak per alert. The glass exists because something real moves behind it; panes blur a defocused field drawn from the same live data as the river, so the background is never decoration.

The system is a working monitor, not a showcase. Density is moderate: a 76px rail, a 64px header, a 236px river, then glass panes, lists and tables in 13-14px type. One family, Red Hat Text, carries everything; its mono cut appears only for data. Night (dark) and day haze (light) share every token name; only the values change, and the day theme dims the glow rather than removing it.

Colour is spent on state, never on chrome. The interface itself is ink on glass; the only saturated colour on screen is a light that means something.
keyCharacteristics: Frosted glass panes (26px blur, 140% saturate) over a live, defocused field of the notifier's own traffic.
Four lights carry all meaning: headlight white (clean), teal (ok, live), sodium amber (waiting, uncertain, error), tail-light red (alert).
One typeface family; mono only for times, IDs, axis ticks, scores and key hints.
Hairline edges instead of dividers with weight; depth from blur and a single soft drop shadow.
Motion is the data moving: 5s linear drift, blurred arrival that settles, and nothing animates under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Tail-Light Rule
rules.body: In the traffic (river, field, feed, trace, mark) red means an alert and nothing else; errors in the traffic are amber. Outside the traffic, the red family appears only where the associate must act: an unreviewed count, a false-alarm verdict, the notifier down, a failed load.

rules.name: The Lights-Are-States Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour appears only as a signal light or the text that names it. Chrome, navigation and headings stay ink on glass; the primary button is filled with ink, not with a hue.

rules.name: The Shared-Name Rule
rules.body: Night and day define the same token names. A new surface uses tokens, never a theme-specific literal, so the switch changes every value at once.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Red Hat Text and its mono cut only. No second display face.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Mono is set on times, IDs, ticket numbers, axis ticks, scores and key hints, never on prose, labels or headings. Labels stay sentence case; there is no uppercase tracking anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The Something-Behind-The-Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass is only used over the live field. If a surface has nothing moving behind it, it does not need more blur; the field supplies the reason for the material.

rules.name: The Blur Ladder Rule
rules.body: Panes blur 26px (with 140% saturate), the rail 22px, tooltips and the sticky feed head 20px, the header 18px over a 55% ground wash.

dos: Do colour every light with the outcome mapping: clean for a quiet check, ok for a passed one, wait for skipped, uncertain or errored, alert for alerts only.
Do put every raised surface on glass (glass, 1px edge, 18px radius for panes) over the live field.
Do set times, IDs and numbers in Red Hat Mono with tabular numerals, and everything else in Red Hat Text.
Do scale every glow by the theme's glow factor (1 at night, 0.55 by day) so day haze stays calm.
Do guard every animation with prefers-reduced-motion; the river and field stop drifting, arrivals and shimmer stop.
Do keep the primary action an ink-filled button, not a coloured one.
donts: Don't use red in the traffic for anything but an alert; errors in the traffic are amber.
Don't place lights that don't stand for real traffic. The gate's still field is the one stand-in, because there is no data before sign-in.
Don't add a second typeface or set prose, labels or headings in mono.
Don't use opaque cards, heavy borders or hard shadows; depth is blur plus the one soft pane lift.
Don't write a theme-specific colour literal into a component; define the token in both themes.
